And His words: ﴿Then We reduced him to the lowest of the low﴾

The interpreters differed concerning the interpretation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: Then We returned him to the lowest age.

Those who said this:

- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi related to us, from Dawud, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿Then We reduced him to the lowest of the low﴾, he said: "To the lowest age."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm related to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAsim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿Then We reduced him to the lowest of the low﴾, he said: "To the lowest age."
- Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿Then We reduced him to the lowest of the low﴾, he says: "He is returned to the lowest age: he grows old until his mind is gone. They were a group who were returned to the lowest age in the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and the Messenger of God ﷺ was asked when their minds had become senile, so God sent down their excuse, that their reward for what they did before their minds departed is theirs."

⁕ Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Abu Rajaʾ, who said: ʿIkrima was asked about His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾. He said: They are returned to the lowest age (arhal al-ʿumr).

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muʾammal and ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, the two of them saying: Sufyan told us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾. He said: To the lowest age.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, the same.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, the same.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾. He said: We return him to senility (al-haram).

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Qatada, who said: Senility (al-haram).

⁕ Yaʿqub related to me, saying: al-Muʿtamir told us, saying: I heard al-Hakam narrate, from ʿIkrima, regarding ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: The aged elder in senility; his old age does not harm him if Allah concludes his life with the best of what he used to do.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Then We return him to the Fire in the most hideous form.

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, from Abu al-ʿAliya, regarding ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: In the worst form, in the form of a pig.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: The Fire.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: To the Fire.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: In the Fire.

⁕ He said: Muʾammal told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: To the Fire.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: Al-Hasan said: Hell is his abode.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, who said: al-Hasan said, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: In the Fire.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: To the Fire.

The most correct of these opinions in my view, and the closest to the interpretation of the verse, is the view of those who said: its meaning is: Then We return him to the lowest age, to the age of the senile (al-kharfa), whose minds have departed due to decrepitude and old age. So he is among the lowest of the low in the decline of life and the departure of intellect.

We said this view is more correct in its interpretation because Allah, may He be remembered, informed about the creation of the son of Adam and His changing him through conditions, as an argument against those who deny His power to resurrect after death. Do you not see that He says: ﴿So what makes you deny the Judgment after this?﴾, meaning: after these proofs.

It is impossible to argue against a people who deny a matter by means of that which they deny. The proof against every people is only by what they cannot repel, what they witness and perceive, or what they acknowledge even if they have not experienced it.

Given that this is so, and that these people denied the Fire with which Allah threatened them in the Hereafter, while they were witnesses to the people of senility and decrepitude after youth and vigor, it is known that He argued against them only with what they were witnessing: His changing His creation, and His moving them from the state of good proportion, youth and vigor, to senility, weakness, the ending of life, and the onset of dementia.

As for His saying: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of this exception. Some of them said: It is a true exception from His saying ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾. They said: The exception of those who believe and do righteous deeds, though they are plural, is permissible from the pronoun in His saying ﴿We return him﴾, which refers to man (al-insan), and man is in singular form; yet although al-insan is in a singular form, it carries the meaning of the plural, since it means the species, as it is said: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss﴾. They said: Likewise it is permissible to say: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾, so that the comparative form (af'al) is added to a group. They said: Had it been intended as a specific single individual, that would not be permissible, just as one does not say "this is more excellent of two standing," but one says "this is more excellent [singular] standing."

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam told us, from Saʿid ibn Sabiq, from ʿAsim al-Ahwal, from ʿIkrima, who said: Whoever recites the Qur'an will not be returned to the lowest age. Then he recited: ﴿Indeed We created man in the best stature, then We returned him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. He said: He will not reach the stage where he knows nothing after having known. According to this interpretation, His saying ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾ refers to a specific group of people, not including those who believe and do righteous deeds, since they are excepted from them.

Others said: Rather, those who believe and do righteous deeds may be included among those who are returned to the lowest of the low, since the lowest age may come upon both the believer and the disbeliever. They said: The exception of His saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ is from an implied meaning in His saying ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾. They said: Its meaning is: Then We return him to the lowest of the low, so their minds depart, they become senile, and their deeds cease, so no good deed is established for them thereafter, ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, for what they used to do of good while their minds were sound and their bodies healthy continues to be recorded for them after their decrepitude and senility.

It is possible that His saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati'), since it is fitting to say: Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward that is not cut off, after he is returned to the lowest of the low.

Those who said the meaning of this view:

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy told us, from Dawud, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾. He said: Whatever man used to do a righteous deed while he was strong and young, then became unable to do it, the reward of that deed continues for him until he dies.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾. He says: If one used to act in obedience to Allah throughout his youth, then grew old until his mind departed, there is recorded for him the like of the righteous deed he used to do in his youth, and he is not held accountable for anything he did in his old age and loss of mind, because he was a believer and used to obey Allah in his youth.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muʾammal told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: To the lowest age. So when the believer reaches the lowest age, there is recorded for him as the best of what he used to do in his youth and health, and this is His saying: (for them is a reward that is not cut off).

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: Then there is recorded for him a reward like what he used to do in health.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ibrahim, the same.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: He said: When one reaches such old age that he is unable to act, there is recorded for him what he used to do.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: their good deeds are recorded for them and their evil deeds are overlooked for them.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam told us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAsim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. He said: They are those whom old age overtook; they are not held accountable for deeds they did in their old age, when they were senile and did not understand.

⁕ Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Abu Rajaʾ, who said: ʿIkrima was asked about His saying: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾. He said: Allah will give him his reward or his deed in full, and will not hold him accountable when he is returned to the lowest age.

⁕ Yaʿqub related to me, saying: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman told us, saying: I heard al-Hakam narrate, from ʿIkrima: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. He said: The aged elder in senility; his old age does not harm him if Allah concludes his life with the best of what he used to do.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. He said: Whoever reaches senility, and used to do righteous deeds, has a reward like his reward while he was able to act.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Then We return him to the lowest of the low in Hell, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward that is not cut off. According to this interpretation, ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ is an exception from the pronoun in His saying ﴿We return him﴾, and their exception from it is permissible since it refers to man, which carries the meaning of the plural, as He said: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe﴾: Except whoever believes.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, who said: al-Hasan said, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: In the Fire. ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: al-Hasan said: It is like His saying: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾.

The most correct of these opinions in our view is the view of those who said: its meaning is: Then We return him to the lowest age, except those who believed and did righteous deeds in their health and youth, for them is a reward that is not cut off after their decrepitude, like what they had of that for their deeds while they were doing them, when they were strong in action.

We said this is more correct due to what we have described as evidence for the soundness of the view that the interpretation of His saying ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾ is the lowest age.

The scholars differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿not cut off﴾. Some of them said: Its meaning is: For them is a reward that is not diminished.

Those who said that:

⁕ ʿAli related to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Muʿawiya told me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾: He says: not diminished.

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: not counted.

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾: not counted.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muʾammal told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾, he said: not counted.

⁕ He said: Sufyan told us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: ﴿for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾, he said: not counted.

It has been said also that the meaning of that is: for them is a reward that is not interrupted.

The most correct of the sayings in this regard is the saying of the one who said: for them is a reward that is not diminished, as it was for them during their health and youth; and this, in my view, derives from their saying: "a mountain that is mannun," meaning when it is weak. From this is the poet's verse:

They gave Hunayda, driven by eight camels, and in their gifts there is neither reproach (mann) nor excess (israf).

[Narrated by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir 1:128, "al-Sirat al-Wadih."]

Meaning: there is in it no deficiency and no fault.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 95, verses 1–6 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His words, mighty and exalted is His name: ﴿By the fig and the olive (1), and by Mount Sinin (2), and by this secure city (3), We have certainly created man in the best of stature (4). Then We reduced him to the lowest of the low (5), except for those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward uninterrupted (6).﴾

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of His words: ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾. Some of them said: By "the fig" is meant the fig that is eaten, and by "the olive" the olive that is pressed.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Rawh related to us, saying: ʿAwf related to us, from al-Hasan, concerning the words of God: ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, he said: "Your fig, this one that is eaten, and your olive, this one that is pressed."
- Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Hakam narrate, from ʿIkrimah, who said: "The fig: it is the fig, and the olive: that which you eat."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, from Yazid, from ʿIkrimah, concerning ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, he said: "Your fig and your olive."
- Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', who said: ʿIkrimah was asked about His words ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, and he said: "The fig is this fig of yours, and the olive is this olive of yours."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, he said: "The fig that is eaten, and the olive: that which is pressed."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us; and Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, all of them from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of God ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, he said: "The fruit that people eat."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Salam ibn Salim, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, he said: "It is your fig and your olive."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, concerning His words ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, he said: "The fig that is eaten, and the olive that is pressed."
- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Kalbi, ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾: "It is that which you see."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan said, concerning His words ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾: "The fig is your fig, and the olive is this your olive."

Others said: The fig is the Mosque of Damascus, and the olive is Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis).

Those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Rawh related to us, saying: ʿAwf related to us, from Yazid Abu ʿAbd Allah, from Kaʿb, that he said concerning the words of God ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾: "The fig: the Mosque of Damascus, and the olive: Jerusalem."
- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿And the fig﴾, he said: "The mountain upon which Damascus stands." ﴿And the olive﴾: "That upon which Jerusalem stands."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾: it was mentioned to us that the fig is the mountain upon which Damascus stands, and the olive is that upon which Jerusalem stands.
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, and I asked him about the words of God ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, he said: "The fig: the Mosque of Damascus, and the olive: the Mosque of Iliya'."
- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Abu Bakr, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, he said: "They are two mountains."

Others said: The fig is the Mosque of Noah, and the olive is the Mosque of Jerusalem.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾: "It means the Mosque of Noah, which was built on al-Judi, and the olive is Jerusalem." He said: "It is said: the fig, the olive, and Mount Sinin are three mosques in al-Sham."

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is the view of those who said: The fig is the fig that is eaten, and the olive is the olive from which oil is pressed, because this is what is well known among the Arabs, and no mountain is known to be called "fig," nor a mountain called "olive," unless someone says: "Our Lord, mighty is His praise, swore by the fig and the olive." The meaning of the speech is an oath by the places where figs grow and the places where olives grow, and this is a valid position, even though there is no clear indication in the apparent text of the revelation that it is so, nor from the statement of anyone whose opposition is not permitted, because Damascus has places where figs grow, and Jerusalem has places where olives grow.

* *

And His words: ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾

The interpreters differed concerning its interpretation. Some of them said: It is the mountain of Musa ibn ʿImran, upon him be God's blessings and peace, and his mosque.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muʿadh ibn Hisham related to us, saying: my father related to me, from Qatadah, from Qaza'ah, who said: I said to Ibn ʿUmar: "I want to go to Jerusalem." [He said:] "Do not go to Mount Sinin; you do not wish to leave the trace of a prophet without treading upon it." Qatadah said: "﴿Mount Sinin﴾: the mosque of Musa ﷺ."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Rawh related to us, saying: ʿAwf related to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His words ﴿Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "The mountain of Musa."
- ʿAwf related to us, from Yazid Abu ʿAbd Allah, from Kaʿb, concerning His words ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "The mountain of Musa ﷺ."
- Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "It is the Tur."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "The mosque of the Tur."

Others said: The Tur is every mountain that produces vegetation.

* *

And His words ﴿Sinin﴾: it is good.

Those who said this:

- ʿImran ibn Musa al-Qazzaz related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Warith ibn Saʿid related to us, saying: ʿAmarah related to us, from ʿIkrimah, concerning His words ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "It means good, and it is the language of Abyssinia; they say of a good thing: 'Sina, sina.'"
- Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', who said: ʿIkrimah was asked about His words ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, and he said: "Tur: a mountain; and Sinin: good, in Abyssinian."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: al-Sabbah ibn Mihrab related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymun, who said: "I prayed behind ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, the Maghrib prayer, and he recited in the first rak'ah ﴿By the fig and the olive, and Mount Sinin﴾." He said: "It is a mountain."
- Yaʿqub related to me, saying: al-Muʿtamir related to us, saying: I heard al-Hakam narrate from ʿIkrimah ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "The plant of the plain and the mountain are alike to me."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "The mountain."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾: "A mountain."
- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾: "The mountain."
- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from al-Nadr, from ʿIkrimah, who said: "The Tur: the mountain, and Sinin: good, just as it grows in the plain, so it grows in the mountain."
- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Kalbi, as for ﴿Tur Sinin﴾, it is the mountain with trees.

Others said: It is the mountain, and they said: Sinin: blessed and good.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿And Tur﴾: the mountain, and ﴿Sinin﴾, he said: "the blessed."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "A blessed mountain in al-Sham."
- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "A mountain in al-Sham, blessed and good."

The most correct of the views on this matter is the view of those who said: Tur Sinin is a known mountain, because the Tur is the mountain with vegetation, so its being attributed to Sinin is a definition of it; and if it were a description of the Tur, as those who said its meaning is "good" or "blessed" said, the Tur would be indefinite (nunnated), because a thing is not attributed to its own description without a reason calling for that.

* *

And His words: ﴿And by this secure city﴾

He says: "And this city, secure from its enemies, that they should fight its people or raid them." It has been said: "al-Amin" means "al-Aman" (the secure), as the poet said:

*Did you not know, O Asma, woe to you, that I*
*Have sworn an oath that I will not betray my trust [amini]*[[Not in his diwan. Al-Qurtubi attributed it in his tafsir (1:128) to ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl, but it is not in his diwan. If it is Hudhali, perhaps it is from the poetry of al-Mutanakhkhil, who has a qasida in Diwan al-Hudhaliyyin 2:18–28 on this rhyme. Also, ʿAmr ibn Maʿdi Karib has similar verses which al-Qali related in al-Nawadir 3:191.]]

He means: "secure" (amini). This is as His words, mighty is His praise, say: ﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure, while people are snatched away from around them?﴾

What is meant by His words ﴿And this secure city﴾ is Mecca.

The interpreters said what we have said in this matter.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His words ﴿And this secure city﴾, he said: "Mecca."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Rawh related to us, saying: ʿAwf related to us, from Yazid Abu ʿAbd Allah, from Kaʿb, concerning the words of God ﴿And this secure city﴾, he said: "The sacred city."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Rawh related to us, saying: ʿAwf related to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His words ﴿And this secure city﴾, he said: "The sacred city."
- He said: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us; and Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan; and Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿And this secure city﴾, he said: "Mecca."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Salam ibn Salim, from Khusayf, from Mujahid: ﴿And this secure city﴾: "Mecca."
- Yaʿqub related to me, saying: al-Muʿtamir related to us, saying: I heard al-Hakam narrate from ʿIkrimah ﴿And this secure city﴾, he said: "The sacred city."
- He said: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', who said: ʿIkrimah was asked about His words ﴿And this secure city﴾, and he said: "Mecca."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah ﴿And this secure city﴾: "He means Mecca."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿And this secure city﴾, he said: "The Sacred Mosque."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim ﴿And this secure city﴾: "Mecca."

* *

And His words: ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾

This is the answer to the oath. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "By the fig and the olive, We have certainly created man in the best of stature."

The interpreters said what we have said in this matter.

Those who said this:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, who said: "The oath occurs here: ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾."

The interpreters differed concerning the interpretation of His words (We have certainly created man in the best of stature). Some of them said: Its meaning is: in the most balanced creation and the finest form.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAsim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿in the best of stature﴾, he said: "In the most balanced creation."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾, he said: "In the best form."
- He said: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, the like of it.
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim ﴿in the best of stature﴾, he said: "Creation."
- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾, he said: "In the best form."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ, from Abu al-ʿAliyah ﴿in the best of stature﴾: he says: "In the best form."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿in the best of stature﴾: "In the best form."
- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾, he said: "The best creation."
- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his words ﴿in the best of stature﴾, he said: "In the best creation."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah ﴿in the best of stature﴾, he says: "In the best form."
- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, and al-Kalbi ﴿in the best of stature﴾, they both said: "In the best form."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: We created man, and We brought him to the prime of his youth, his vigor and his strength, when he is at his best, most balanced, and most upright.

Those who said this:

- Yaʿqub related to me, saying: al-Muʿtamir related to us, saying: I heard al-Hakam narrate, from ʿIkrimah, concerning His words ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾, he said: "The strong, vigorous young man."
- Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾, he said: "His youth, at the first of his growing up."

Others said: It was said this way because there is no living creature except that it walks prone on its face, other than man.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi related to us, from Dawud, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾, he said: "Every thing was created prone on its face, except man."

The most correct view regarding this, in our judgment, is to say: the meaning is: We have certainly created man in the best form and the most balanced of forms; because His words ﴿best of stature﴾ are only a description of something omitted, which is "in a stature, the best stature," so it is as if it were said: "We have certainly created him in a stature, the best of stature."

* *

And His words: ﴿Then We reduced him to the lowest of the low﴾

The interpreters differed concerning the interpretation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: Then We returned him to the lowest age.

Those who said this:

- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi related to us, from Dawud, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿Then We reduced him to the lowest of the low﴾, he said: "To the lowest age."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm related to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAsim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿Then We reduced him to the lowest of the low﴾, he said: "To the lowest age."
- Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿Then We reduced him to the lowest of the low﴾, he says: "He is returned to the lowest age: he grows old until his mind is gone. They were a group who were returned to the lowest age in the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and the Messenger of God ﷺ was asked when their minds had become senile, so God sent down their excuse, that their reward for what they did before their minds departed is theirs."

⁕ Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Abu Rajaʾ, who said: ʿIkrima was asked about His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾. He said: They are returned to the lowest age (arhal al-ʿumr).

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muʾammal and ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, the two of them saying: Sufyan told us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾. He said: To the lowest age.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, the same.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, the same.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾. He said: We return him to senility (al-haram).

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Qatada, who said: Senility (al-haram).

⁕ Yaʿqub related to me, saying: al-Muʿtamir told us, saying: I heard al-Hakam narrate, from ʿIkrima, regarding ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: The aged elder in senility; his old age does not harm him if Allah concludes his life with the best of what he used to do.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Then We return him to the Fire in the most hideous form.

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, from Abu al-ʿAliya, regarding ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: In the worst form, in the form of a pig.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: The Fire.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: To the Fire.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: In the Fire.

⁕ He said: Muʾammal told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: To the Fire.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: Al-Hasan said: Hell is his abode.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, who said: al-Hasan said, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: In the Fire.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: To the Fire.

The most correct of these opinions in my view, and the closest to the interpretation of the verse, is the view of those who said: its meaning is: Then We return him to the lowest age, to the age of the senile (al-kharfa), whose minds have departed due to decrepitude and old age. So he is among the lowest of the low in the decline of life and the departure of intellect.

We said this view is more correct in its interpretation because Allah, may He be remembered, informed about the creation of the son of Adam and His changing him through conditions, as an argument against those who deny His power to resurrect after death. Do you not see that He says: ﴿So what makes you deny the Judgment after this?﴾, meaning: after these proofs.

It is impossible to argue against a people who deny a matter by means of that which they deny. The proof against every people is only by what they cannot repel, what they witness and perceive, or what they acknowledge even if they have not experienced it.

Given that this is so, and that these people denied the Fire with which Allah threatened them in the Hereafter, while they were witnesses to the people of senility and decrepitude after youth and vigor, it is known that He argued against them only with what they were witnessing: His changing His creation, and His moving them from the state of good proportion, youth and vigor, to senility, weakness, the ending of life, and the onset of dementia.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of this exception. Some of them said: It is a true exception from His saying ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾. They said: The exception of those who believe and do righteous deeds, though they are plural, is permissible from the pronoun in His saying ﴿We return him﴾, which refers to man (al-insan), and man is in singular form; yet although al-insan is in a singular form, it carries the meaning of the plural, since it means the species, as it is said: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss﴾. They said: Likewise it is permissible to say: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾, so that the comparative form (af'al) is added to a group. They said: Had it been intended as a specific single individual, that would not be permissible, just as one does not say "this is more excellent of two standing," but one says "this is more excellent [singular] standing."

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam told us, from Saʿid ibn Sabiq, from ʿAsim al-Ahwal, from ʿIkrima, who said: Whoever recites the Qur'an will not be returned to the lowest age. Then he recited: ﴿Indeed We created man in the best stature, then We returned him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. He said: He will not reach the stage where he knows nothing after having known. According to this interpretation, His saying ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾ refers to a specific group of people, not including those who believe and do righteous deeds, since they are excepted from them.

Others said: Rather, those who believe and do righteous deeds may be included among those who are returned to the lowest of the low, since the lowest age may come upon both the believer and the disbeliever. They said: The exception of His saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ is from an implied meaning in His saying ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾. They said: Its meaning is: Then We return him to the lowest of the low, so their minds depart, they become senile, and their deeds cease, so no good deed is established for them thereafter, ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, for what they used to do of good while their minds were sound and their bodies healthy continues to be recorded for them after their decrepitude and senility.

It is possible that His saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati'), since it is fitting to say: Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward that is not cut off, after he is returned to the lowest of the low.

Those who said the meaning of this view:

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy told us, from Dawud, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾. He said: Whatever man used to do a righteous deed while he was strong and young, then became unable to do it, the reward of that deed continues for him until he dies.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾. He says: If one used to act in obedience to Allah throughout his youth, then grew old until his mind departed, there is recorded for him the like of the righteous deed he used to do in his youth, and he is not held accountable for anything he did in his old age and loss of mind, because he was a believer and used to obey Allah in his youth.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muʾammal told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: To the lowest age. So when the believer reaches the lowest age, there is recorded for him as the best of what he used to do in his youth and health, and this is His saying: (for them is a reward that is not cut off).

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: Then there is recorded for him a reward like what he used to do in health.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ibrahim, the same.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: He said: When one reaches such old age that he is unable to act, there is recorded for him what he used to do.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: their good deeds are recorded for them and their evil deeds are overlooked for them.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam told us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAsim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. He said: They are those whom old age overtook; they are not held accountable for deeds they did in their old age, when they were senile and did not understand.

⁕ Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Abu Rajaʾ, who said: ʿIkrima was asked about His saying: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾. He said: Allah will give him his reward or his deed in full, and will not hold him accountable when he is returned to the lowest age.

⁕ Yaʿqub related to me, saying: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman told us, saying: I heard al-Hakam narrate, from ʿIkrima: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. He said: The aged elder in senility; his old age does not harm him if Allah concludes his life with the best of what he used to do.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. He said: Whoever reaches senility, and used to do righteous deeds, has a reward like his reward while he was able to act.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Then We return him to the lowest of the low in Hell, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward that is not cut off. According to this interpretation, ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ is an exception from the pronoun in His saying ﴿We return him﴾, and their exception from it is permissible since it refers to man, which carries the meaning of the plural, as He said: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe﴾: Except whoever believes.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, who said: al-Hasan said, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: In the Fire. ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: al-Hasan said: It is like His saying: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾.

The most correct of these opinions in our view is the view of those who said: its meaning is: Then We return him to the lowest age, except those who believed and did righteous deeds in their health and youth, for them is a reward that is not cut off after their decrepitude, like what they had of that for their deeds while they were doing them, when they were strong in action.

We said this is more correct due to what we have described as evidence for the soundness of the view that the interpretation of His saying ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾ is the lowest age.

The scholars differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿not cut off﴾. Some of them said: Its meaning is: For them is a reward that is not diminished.

Those who said that:

⁕ ʿAli related to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Muʿawiya told me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾: He says: not diminished.

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: not counted.

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾: not counted.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muʾammal told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾, he said: not counted.

⁕ He said: Sufyan told us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: ﴿for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾, he said: not counted.

It has been said also that the meaning of that is: for them is a reward that is not interrupted.

The most correct of the sayings in this regard is the saying of the one who said: for them is a reward that is not diminished, as it was for them during their health and youth; and this, in my view, derives from their saying: "a mountain that is mannun," meaning when it is weak. From this is the poet's verse:

They gave Hunayda, driven by eight camels, and in their gifts there is neither reproach (mann) nor excess (israf).

[Narrated by al-Qurtubi in his tafsir 1:128, "al-Sirat al-Wadih."]

Meaning: there is in it no deficiency and no fault.

Commentary of al-Tabari (Jami al-Bayan) on surah 95, verses 1–6 (part 1 of 2):

The interpretation of His words, mighty and exalted is His name: ﴿By the fig and the olive (1), and by Mount Sinin (2), and by this secure city (3), We have certainly created man in the best of stature (4). Then We reduced him to the lowest of the low (5), except for those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward uninterrupted (6).﴾

The interpreters differed concerning the meaning of His words: ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾. Some of them said: By "the fig" is meant the fig that is eaten, and by "the olive" the olive that is pressed.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Rawh related to us, saying: ʿAwf related to us, from al-Hasan, concerning the words of God: ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, he said: "Your fig, this one that is eaten, and your olive, this one that is pressed."
- Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim related to me, saying: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman related to us, saying: I heard al-Hakam narrate, from ʿIkrimah, who said: "The fig: it is the fig, and the olive: that which you eat."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Yahya ibn Wadih related to us, saying: al-Husayn related to us, from Yazid, from ʿIkrimah, concerning ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, he said: "Your fig and your olive."
- Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', who said: ʿIkrimah was asked about His words ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, and he said: "The fig is this fig of yours, and the olive is this olive of yours."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, he said: "The fig that is eaten, and the olive: that which is pressed."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us; and Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, all of them from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning the words of God ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, he said: "The fruit that people eat."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Salam ibn Salim, from Khusayf, from Mujahid, ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, he said: "It is your fig and your olive."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, concerning His words ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, he said: "The fig that is eaten, and the olive that is pressed."
- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Kalbi, ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾: "It is that which you see."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan said, concerning His words ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾: "The fig is your fig, and the olive is this your olive."

Others said: The fig is the Mosque of Damascus, and the olive is Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis).

Those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Rawh related to us, saying: ʿAwf related to us, from Yazid Abu ʿAbd Allah, from Kaʿb, that he said concerning the words of God ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾: "The fig: the Mosque of Damascus, and the olive: Jerusalem."
- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, concerning His words ﴿And the fig﴾, he said: "The mountain upon which Damascus stands." ﴿And the olive﴾: "That upon which Jerusalem stands."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾: it was mentioned to us that the fig is the mountain upon which Damascus stands, and the olive is that upon which Jerusalem stands.
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, and I asked him about the words of God ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, he said: "The fig: the Mosque of Damascus, and the olive: the Mosque of Iliya'."
- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Abu Bakr, from ʿIkrimah: ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾, he said: "They are two mountains."

Others said: The fig is the Mosque of Noah, and the olive is the Mosque of Jerusalem.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, concerning His words ﴿And the fig and the olive﴾: "It means the Mosque of Noah, which was built on al-Judi, and the olive is Jerusalem." He said: "It is said: the fig, the olive, and Mount Sinin are three mosques in al-Sham."

The correct view on this matter, in our opinion, is the view of those who said: The fig is the fig that is eaten, and the olive is the olive from which oil is pressed, because this is what is well known among the Arabs, and no mountain is known to be called "fig," nor a mountain called "olive," unless someone says: "Our Lord, mighty is His praise, swore by the fig and the olive." The meaning of the speech is an oath by the places where figs grow and the places where olives grow, and this is a valid position, even though there is no clear indication in the apparent text of the revelation that it is so, nor from the statement of anyone whose opposition is not permitted, because Damascus has places where figs grow, and Jerusalem has places where olives grow.

* *

And His words: ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾

The interpreters differed concerning its interpretation. Some of them said: It is the mountain of Musa ibn ʿImran, upon him be God's blessings and peace, and his mosque.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muʿadh ibn Hisham related to us, saying: my father related to me, from Qatadah, from Qaza'ah, who said: I said to Ibn ʿUmar: "I want to go to Jerusalem." [He said:] "Do not go to Mount Sinin; you do not wish to leave the trace of a prophet without treading upon it." Qatadah said: "﴿Mount Sinin﴾: the mosque of Musa ﷺ."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Rawh related to us, saying: ʿAwf related to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His words ﴿Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "The mountain of Musa."
- ʿAwf related to us, from Yazid Abu ʿAbd Allah, from Kaʿb, concerning His words ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "The mountain of Musa ﷺ."
- Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "It is the Tur."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "The mosque of the Tur."

Others said: The Tur is every mountain that produces vegetation.

* *

And His words ﴿Sinin﴾: it is good.

Those who said this:

- ʿImran ibn Musa al-Qazzaz related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Warith ibn Saʿid related to us, saying: ʿAmarah related to us, from ʿIkrimah, concerning His words ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "It means good, and it is the language of Abyssinia; they say of a good thing: 'Sina, sina.'"
- Yaʿqub ibn Ibrahim related to us, saying: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', who said: ʿIkrimah was asked about His words ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, and he said: "Tur: a mountain; and Sinin: good, in Abyssinian."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: al-Sabbah ibn Mihrab related to us, from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from ʿAmr ibn Maymun, who said: "I prayed behind ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, the Maghrib prayer, and he recited in the first rak'ah ﴿By the fig and the olive, and Mount Sinin﴾." He said: "It is a mountain."
- Yaʿqub related to me, saying: al-Muʿtamir related to us, saying: I heard al-Hakam narrate from ʿIkrimah ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "The plant of the plain and the mountain are alike to me."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "The mountain."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾: "A mountain."
- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾: "The mountain."
- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from al-Nadr, from ʿIkrimah, who said: "The Tur: the mountain, and Sinin: good, just as it grows in the plain, so it grows in the mountain."
- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from al-Kalbi, as for ﴿Tur Sinin﴾, it is the mountain with trees.

Others said: It is the mountain, and they said: Sinin: blessed and good.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿And Tur﴾: the mountain, and ﴿Sinin﴾, he said: "the blessed."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "A blessed mountain in al-Sham."
- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah ﴿And Mount Sinin﴾, he said: "A mountain in al-Sham, blessed and good."

The most correct of the views on this matter is the view of those who said: Tur Sinin is a known mountain, because the Tur is the mountain with vegetation, so its being attributed to Sinin is a definition of it; and if it were a description of the Tur, as those who said its meaning is "good" or "blessed" said, the Tur would be indefinite (nunnated), because a thing is not attributed to its own description without a reason calling for that.

* *

And His words: ﴿And by this secure city﴾

He says: "And this city, secure from its enemies, that they should fight its people or raid them." It has been said: "al-Amin" means "al-Aman" (the secure), as the poet said:

*Did you not know, O Asma, woe to you, that I*
*Have sworn an oath that I will not betray my trust [amini]*[[Not in his diwan. Al-Qurtubi attributed it in his tafsir (1:128) to ʿAmir ibn al-Tufayl, but it is not in his diwan. If it is Hudhali, perhaps it is from the poetry of al-Mutanakhkhil, who has a qasida in Diwan al-Hudhaliyyin 2:18–28 on this rhyme. Also, ʿAmr ibn Maʿdi Karib has similar verses which al-Qali related in al-Nawadir 3:191.]]

He means: "secure" (amini). This is as His words, mighty is His praise, say: ﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure, while people are snatched away from around them?﴾

What is meant by His words ﴿And this secure city﴾ is Mecca.

The interpreters said what we have said in this matter.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas, His words ﴿And this secure city﴾, he said: "Mecca."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Rawh related to us, saying: ʿAwf related to us, from Yazid Abu ʿAbd Allah, from Kaʿb, concerning the words of God ﴿And this secure city﴾, he said: "The sacred city."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Rawh related to us, saying: ʿAwf related to us, from al-Hasan, concerning His words ﴿And this secure city﴾, he said: "The sacred city."
- He said: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us; and Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan; and Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿And this secure city﴾, he said: "Mecca."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the like of it.
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Salam ibn Salim, from Khusayf, from Mujahid: ﴿And this secure city﴾: "Mecca."
- Yaʿqub related to me, saying: al-Muʿtamir related to us, saying: I heard al-Hakam narrate from ʿIkrimah ﴿And this secure city﴾, he said: "The sacred city."
- He said: Ibn ʿUlayyah related to us, from Abu Raja', who said: ʿIkrimah was asked about His words ﴿And this secure city﴾, and he said: "Mecca."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah ﴿And this secure city﴾: "He means Mecca."
- Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, concerning His words ﴿And this secure city﴾, he said: "The Sacred Mosque."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim ﴿And this secure city﴾: "Mecca."

* *

And His words: ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾

This is the answer to the oath. He, may His remembrance be exalted, says: "By the fig and the olive, We have certainly created man in the best of stature."

The interpreters said what we have said in this matter.

Those who said this:

- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah, who said: "The oath occurs here: ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾."

The interpreters differed concerning the interpretation of His words (We have certainly created man in the best of stature). Some of them said: Its meaning is: in the most balanced creation and the finest form.

Those who said this:

- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam related to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAsim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿in the best of stature﴾, he said: "In the most balanced creation."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾, he said: "In the best form."
- He said: ʿAbd al-Rahman related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, the like of it.
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim ﴿in the best of stature﴾, he said: "Creation."
- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾, he said: "In the best form."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran related to us, from Abu Jaʿfar, from al-Rabiʿ, from Abu al-ʿAliyah ﴿in the best of stature﴾: he says: "In the best form."
- Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Mu'ammal related to us, saying: Sufyan related to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿in the best of stature﴾: "In the best form."
- Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' related to us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾, he said: "The best creation."
- Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim related to us, saying: ʿIsa related to us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan related to us, saying: Warqa' related to us, all of them from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, his words ﴿in the best of stature﴾, he said: "In the best creation."
- Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid related to us, saying: Saʿid related to us, from Qatadah ﴿in the best of stature﴾, he says: "In the best form."
- Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr related to us, from Maʿmar, from Qatadah, and al-Kalbi ﴿in the best of stature﴾, they both said: "In the best form."

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: We created man, and We brought him to the prime of his youth, his vigor and his strength, when he is at his best, most balanced, and most upright.

Those who said this:

- Yaʿqub related to me, saying: al-Muʿtamir related to us, saying: I heard al-Hakam narrate, from ʿIkrimah, concerning His words ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾, he said: "The strong, vigorous young man."
- Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾, he said: "His youth, at the first of his growing up."

Others said: It was said this way because there is no living creature except that it walks prone on its face, other than man.

Those who said this:

- Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi related to us, from Dawud, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿We have certainly created man in the best of stature﴾, he said: "Every thing was created prone on its face, except man."

The most correct view regarding this, in our judgment, is to say: the meaning is: We have certainly created man in the best form and the most balanced of forms; because His words ﴿best of stature﴾ are only a description of something omitted, which is "in a stature, the best stature," so it is as if it were said: "We have certainly created him in a stature, the best of stature."

* *

And His words: ﴿Then We reduced him to the lowest of the low﴾

The interpreters differed concerning the interpretation of that. Some of them said: The meaning of that is: Then We returned him to the lowest age.

Those who said this:

- Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdi related to us, from Dawud, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿Then We reduced him to the lowest of the low﴾, he said: "To the lowest age."
- Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam ibn Salm related to us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAsim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿Then We reduced him to the lowest of the low﴾, he said: "To the lowest age."
- Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: my father related to me, saying: my paternal uncle related to me, saying: my father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas ﴿Then We reduced him to the lowest of the low﴾, he says: "He is returned to the lowest age: he grows old until his mind is gone. They were a group who were returned to the lowest age in the time of the Messenger of God ﷺ, and the Messenger of God ﷺ was asked when their minds had become senile, so God sent down their excuse, that their reward for what they did before their minds departed is theirs."

⁕ Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Abu Rajaʾ, who said: ʿIkrima was asked about His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾. He said: They are returned to the lowest age (arhal al-ʿumr).

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muʾammal and ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, the two of them saying: Sufyan told us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾. He said: To the lowest age.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, the same.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, the same.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾. He said: We return him to senility (al-haram).

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Qatada, who said: Senility (al-haram).

⁕ Yaʿqub related to me, saying: al-Muʿtamir told us, saying: I heard al-Hakam narrate, from ʿIkrima, regarding ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: The aged elder in senility; his old age does not harm him if Allah concludes his life with the best of what he used to do.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Then We return him to the Fire in the most hideous form.

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi, from al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas, from Abu al-ʿAliya, regarding ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: In the worst form, in the form of a pig.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, regarding ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: The Fire.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: To the Fire.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: In the Fire.

⁕ He said: Muʾammal told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, who said: To the Fire.

⁕ Bishr related to us, saying: Yazid told us, saying: Saʿid told us, from Qatada, regarding ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: Al-Hasan said: Hell is his abode.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada, who said: al-Hasan said, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: In the Fire.

⁕ Yunus related to me, saying: Ibn Wahb informed us, saying: Ibn Zayd said, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: To the Fire.

The most correct of these opinions in my view, and the closest to the interpretation of the verse, is the view of those who said: its meaning is: Then We return him to the lowest age, to the age of the senile (al-kharfa), whose minds have departed due to decrepitude and old age. So he is among the lowest of the low in the decline of life and the departure of intellect.

We said this view is more correct in its interpretation because Allah, may He be remembered, informed about the creation of the son of Adam and His changing him through conditions, as an argument against those who deny His power to resurrect after death. Do you not see that He says: ﴿So what makes you deny the Judgment after this?﴾, meaning: after these proofs.

It is impossible to argue against a people who deny a matter by means of that which they deny. The proof against every people is only by what they cannot repel, what they witness and perceive, or what they acknowledge even if they have not experienced it.

Given that this is so, and that these people denied the Fire with which Allah threatened them in the Hereafter, while they were witnesses to the people of senility and decrepitude after youth and vigor, it is known that He argued against them only with what they were witnessing: His changing His creation, and His moving them from the state of good proportion, youth and vigor, to senility, weakness, the ending of life, and the onset of dementia.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾.

The people of interpretation differed regarding the meaning of this exception. Some of them said: It is a true exception from His saying ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾. They said: The exception of those who believe and do righteous deeds, though they are plural, is permissible from the pronoun in His saying ﴿We return him﴾, which refers to man (al-insan), and man is in singular form; yet although al-insan is in a singular form, it carries the meaning of the plural, since it means the species, as it is said: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss﴾. They said: Likewise it is permissible to say: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾, so that the comparative form (af'al) is added to a group. They said: Had it been intended as a specific single individual, that would not be permissible, just as one does not say "this is more excellent of two standing," but one says "this is more excellent [singular] standing."

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam told us, from Saʿid ibn Sabiq, from ʿAsim al-Ahwal, from ʿIkrima, who said: Whoever recites the Qur'an will not be returned to the lowest age. Then he recited: ﴿Indeed We created man in the best stature, then We returned him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. He said: He will not reach the stage where he knows nothing after having known. According to this interpretation, His saying ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾ refers to a specific group of people, not including those who believe and do righteous deeds, since they are excepted from them.

Others said: Rather, those who believe and do righteous deeds may be included among those who are returned to the lowest of the low, since the lowest age may come upon both the believer and the disbeliever. They said: The exception of His saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ is from an implied meaning in His saying ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾. They said: Its meaning is: Then We return him to the lowest of the low, so their minds depart, they become senile, and their deeds cease, so no good deed is established for them thereafter, ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, for what they used to do of good while their minds were sound and their bodies healthy continues to be recorded for them after their decrepitude and senility.

It is possible that His saying ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ is a disjunctive exception (istithna' munqati'), since it is fitting to say: Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds; for them is a reward that is not cut off, after he is returned to the lowest of the low.

Those who said the meaning of this view:

⁕ Ibn al-Muthanna related to us, saying: Ibn Abi ʿAdiyy told us, from Dawud, from ʿIkrima, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾. He said: Whatever man used to do a righteous deed while he was strong and young, then became unable to do it, the reward of that deed continues for him until he dies.

⁕ Muhammad ibn Saʿd related to me, saying: My father told me, saying: My uncle told me, saying: My father told me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾. He says: If one used to act in obedience to Allah throughout his youth, then grew old until his mind departed, there is recorded for him the like of the righteous deed he used to do in his youth, and he is not held accountable for anything he did in his old age and loss of mind, because he was a believer and used to obey Allah in his youth.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muʾammal told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: To the lowest age. So when the believer reaches the lowest age, there is recorded for him as the best of what he used to do in his youth and health, and this is His saying: (for them is a reward that is not cut off).

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: ʿAbd al-Rahman told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: Then there is recorded for him a reward like what he used to do in health.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman, from Ibrahim, the same.

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: He said: When one reaches such old age that he is unable to act, there is recorded for him what he used to do.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: their good deeds are recorded for them and their evil deeds are overlooked for them.

Those who said that:

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Hakkam told us, from ʿAmr, from ʿAsim, from Abu Razin, from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. He said: They are those whom old age overtook; they are not held accountable for deeds they did in their old age, when they were senile and did not understand.

⁕ Yaʿqub related to me, saying: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Abu Rajaʾ, who said: ʿIkrima was asked about His saying: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾. He said: Allah will give him his reward or his deed in full, and will not hold him accountable when he is returned to the lowest age.

⁕ Yaʿqub related to me, saying: al-Muʿtamir ibn Sulayman told us, saying: I heard al-Hakam narrate, from ʿIkrima: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. He said: The aged elder in senility; his old age does not harm him if Allah concludes his life with the best of what he used to do.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatada: ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾. He said: Whoever reaches senility, and used to do righteous deeds, has a reward like his reward while he was able to act.

Others said: Rather, the meaning of that is: Then We return him to the lowest of the low in Hell, except those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them is a reward that is not cut off. According to this interpretation, ﴿except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾ is an exception from the pronoun in His saying ﴿We return him﴾, and their exception from it is permissible since it refers to man, which carries the meaning of the plural, as He said: ﴿Indeed, mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾.

Those who said that:

⁕ Muhammad ibn ʿAmr related to me, saying: Abu ʿAsim told us, saying: ʿIsa told us; and al-Harith related to me, saying: al-Hasan told us, saying: Warqa' told us, both from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low, except those who believe﴾: Except whoever believes.

⁕ Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿla related to us, saying: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, who said: al-Hasan said, regarding His saying: ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾: In the Fire. ﴿Except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾: al-Hasan said: It is like His saying: ﴿By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾.

The most correct of these opinions in our view is the view of those who said: its meaning is: Then We return him to the lowest age, except those who believed and did righteous deeds in their health and youth, for them is a reward that is not cut off after their decrepitude, like what they had of that for their deeds while they were doing them, when they were strong in action.

We said this is more correct due to what we have described as evidence for the soundness of the view that the interpretation of His saying ﴿Then We return him to the lowest of the low﴾ is the lowest age.

The scholars differed regarding the interpretation of His saying: ﴿not cut off﴾. Some of them said: Its meaning is: For them is a reward that is not diminished.

Those who said that:

⁕ ʿAli related to me, saying: Abu Salih told us, saying: Muʿawiya told me, from ʿAli, from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾: He says: not diminished.

Others said: Rather, its meaning is: not counted.

Those who said that:

⁕ Abu Kurayb related to us, saying: Waki' told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Jurayj, from Mujahid: ﴿for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾: not counted.

⁕ Ibn Humayd related to us, saying: Mihran told us, from Sufyan, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, the same.

⁕ Ibn Bashshar related to us, saying: Muʾammal told us, saying: Sufyan told us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: ﴿for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾, he said: not counted.

⁕ He said: Sufyan told us, from Hammad, from Ibrahim: ﴿for them is a reward that is not cut off﴾, he said: not counted.

It has been said also that the meaning of that is: for them is a reward that is not interrupted.

The most correct of the sayings in this regard is the saying of the one who said: for them is a reward that is not diminished, as it was for them during their health and youth; and this, in my view, derives from their saying: "a mountain that is mannun," meaning when it is weak.
